Items.Authors: Christian Ramirez, Constanza Araujo Hauck, Andres González, Gerardo Smith, Jindrich Martinu, Ahmed Miliani, Sébastien Adans, Jeroen Schotsaert
Items.Title: Engineering the ELT’s Reflective Surfaces.
Items.Abstract: The ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) requires a coating facility capable of processing all of its large mirrors—M2, M3, M4, and M5—within a single, industrial-scale system. The Large Coating Plant (LCP) has been designed to support mirrors with convex, concave, and flat geometries of M2, M3, and M5 in a single machine. The magnetron sputtering of a Protected Silver layer serves as the baseline for all ELT mirrors. Still, a dedicated process is implemented for M4, which features magnets on the rear side of its deformable mirror shells, affecting the homogeneity of magnetron sputtering. Hence, M4 receives an evaporated aluminium coating using a purpose-configured evaporation sub-system within the same LCP. This paper presents the capabilities of the LCP, including an overview of acceptance testing and coating performance results, and dedicated work to enhance the reflectivity of the aluminum layer for M4 in a specific band.

Items.Authors: Roberto Tamai, Bertrand Koehler, Joël Vernet, Fabio Biancat-Marchet, Mauro Tuti, Juan-Carlos González-Herrera
Items.Title: ESO’s ELT takes shape: first deliveries and start of AIV
Items.Abstract: The construction of the ESO's Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) passed the 70% completion mark in 2025.     The Programme schedule needed to be redefined in December 2024 due to various delays in the industrial contracts, leading to a telescope first light in March 2029.     However, the progress over the last two years has been impressive. The main activities have shifted from design and manufacturing to acceptance and delivery of major components as well as the start of the Assembly, Integration and Verification (AIV) activities on site.     At the construction site at Armazones (Chile), the Dome and Main Structure took their final external aspect. At the ELT Technical Facility (ETF) at Paranal, the first M1 segments are being coated. In Europe, several industrial contracts could be closed after they completed their respective delivery.    This paper summarizes the achieved progress of the ESO's ELT Construction

Items.Authors: Dominic J. Benford, Jessica Gaskin, Hashima Hasan
Items.Title: How NASA astrophysics supports future technologies and technologists in the era of the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: NASA’s Astrophysics Division features multiple solicitations to fund technology development for future space flight missions. We will present the paradigm used in these solicitations, a compare-and-contrast between the two, and the process for how technologies have been prioritized for inclusion in the SAT opportunity. We have statistics on selections, including groupings by subject matter and how these have evolved over time. Our focus is on the open APRA and SAT programs, and we will also cover the intramural funding for technology development. Over the years, several selected proposals have led to technologies which have been infused into later flight missions. There are now shifting approaches being used to emphasize technology development for the Habitable Worlds Observatory We will discuss anecdotal aspects of NASA’s technology innovation, maturation, and flight pipeline, and how it supports early-career researchers.

Items.Authors: Huaqing Cheng, Haiwu Pan, Zhixing Ling, Chen Zhang, Yuan Liu, Weimin Yuan
Items.Title: In-flight calibration of the wide-field x-ray telescope (WXT) on board the Einstein Probe
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) onboard the Einstein Probe satellite is dedicated to capturing X-ray transients and outbursts of known sources, with an unprecedented combination of a large field of view and high sensitivity. We present the result of the in-flight calibration campaign of WXT. The calibration terms of WXT include the PSF, effective area, and the energy response of the CMOS detectors. The first round of the in-flight calibration campaign started from January 2024 to May 2024. The calibration sources are Crab, Sco X-1, Tycho, and Cas A. Detailed analysis shows that the in-orbit performance is consistent with the on-ground result. The calibration results have been incorporated into the updated version of the calibration database (CALDB) and applied to the analysis of the scientific data of WXT. All of these measurements meet the requirements designed for WXT.

Items.Authors: Kate J. Jackson, Maaike van Kooten, Jean-Pierre Véran, Ed Chapin, Dan Kerley, Simon Carrier
Items.Title: Observing demonstration with the REVOLT AO system
Items.Abstract: Observe the REVOLT! Join us for a live on-sky demonstration of the REVOLT  adaptive optics (AO) system, broadcast from the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory in  Victoria, Canada. REVOLT is operated using the Herzberg Extensible Adaptive  optics Realtime Toolkit (HEART), at speeds up to 1kHz. During the session,  we will close the AO loop with HEART in both Shack–Hartmann and Pyramid  wavefront sensor (WFS) modes, and showcase its soft real-time background  processes, including on-the-fly estimation of r0 and optical gain tracking for  the PWFS. The demonstration will conclude with a live data reduction using  our custom HEART-Analysis tools to derive the system’s Rejection Transfer  Function and compute the Strehl ratio of the science PSF.

Items.Authors: Michael E. Hoenk, Nathan Bush, April D. Jewell, John Hennessy, Charles A. Shapiro, Todd J. Jones, Jesper Skottfelt, David Morris, Christopher S. Moore, Shouleh Nikzad
Items.Title: Physics, performance and deployment of delta-doped sensors for X-ray to ultraviolet imaging and spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: NASA’s goals in precision astrometry and time domain astrophysics require stable, precisely calibrated sensors, and yet UV and X-ray CCDs and CMOS image sensors are susceptible to damage and instabilities caused by the very photons they’re supposed to detect. UV astronomers have been advocating an expansion of the spectral range of the Habitable Worlds Observatory into the far and extreme UV range, where the rates and severity of UV-induced surface damage are severe. Depending on the outcome of the competition, development of x ray detectors will remain critical in the near to mid future. We’ve previously reported that delta-doped detectors are uniquely hardened against the effects of this type of radiation-induced surface damage. In this paper, we will explore the physics and performance of delta-doped detectors based on new data, and we will report our progress on developing and deploying large format delta-doped CCDs and CMOS image sensors for NASA missions.

Items.Authors: Piero Benvenuti
Items.Title: Protecting the dark and quiet sky from satellite constellation interference
Items.Abstract: The exponential increase in the population of satellites in Low Earth Orbit is seriously interfering with optical, infrared and radio astronomical observations. The Centre for the Protection of Dark and Quiet Sky, created by the International Astronomical Union in 2022, is actively engaged in discussions with all concerned stakeholders on possible mitigating measures. While the majority of the current LEO population is represented by communication satellite constellations (Starlink, Amazon/Kuiper, Oneweb, Guowang, Qianfan, etc.), other types of constellations are being planned in LEO, MEO and GEO, especially concerning the transmission of space-collected solar light or solar energy to the ground. The interference of the different types of constellations on astronomy will be discussed, along with possible mitigating measures.

Items.Authors: Vincent Foriel, Marc-Antoine Martinod, David Mary, Frantz Martinache, Nick Cvetojevic, Romain Laugier, Roxanne Ligi, Sylvie Robbe-Dubois, Jeronimo Calderon-Gomez, Frantz Martinache
Items.Title: Tunable kernel-nulling interferometry using active photonics for direct exoplanet detection
Items.Abstract: The direct detection of exoplanets requires instruments delivering extreme contrast, high angular resolution, and long-term stability. Nulling interferometry can meet these requirements if the beam recombiner is actively stabilized. We present the status of a laboratory effort within the PHOTONICS project, focusing on a near-infrared tunable photonic kernel-nulling recombiner for a 4-telescope array. The SiN device provides six nulled outputs and integrates 14 thermo-optic phase shifters (TOPAS) for fine tuning and active cophasing. We demonstrate two calibration strategies that bring the imperfect manufactured chip close to its ideal operating point. The same approach enables shifting the null wavelength, allowing active spectral scanning to target features such as biosignatures. Dedicated signal-processing and statistical tools further support robust detection and astrometric characterization. Finally, we extrapolate these results to VLTI and the proposed space mission LIFE.

Items.Authors: Gavin B. Dalton, David L. Terrett, Scott C. Trager, Don Carlos Abrams, Ian J. Lewis, Sarah L. Hughes, Lilian Dominguez, Shoko Jin, Andrea Henderson de la Fuente, WEAVE Consortium
Items.Title: WEAVE at the William Herschel Telescope: realising the on-sky performance of a 1000-fibre pick-and-place positioning system
Items.Abstract: The new WEAVE facility was deployed on the William Herschel Telescope  in mid-2022 and is expected to be in full science operations in early  2026 with a pick and place positioner capable of deploying up to 1000  optical fibres over the 2 degree prime-focus field of view. Here we  present details of the on- and off-sky calibrations required to ensure  the full astrometric accuracy of the system, including internal  consistency calibrations for the positioning robots, as well as implied flexure  and alignment parameters for the full optical system of telescope,  corrector, field rotator and positioner. We will conclude with some  examples of delivered on-sky data and a summary of some early science results.

Items.Authors: K. Thakurwani, B. Petraitis, M. Brophy
Items.Title: High durability UV-enhanced silver coatings on 0.5m optics: performance, environmental stability, and failure analysis
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the development of high-durability UV-Enhanced silver mirror coatings applied to 0.5-meter class optics. Detailed study of failures driving process optimization enabled high UV reflectance, improved environmental resistance, and consistent coating uniformity across large apertures. Key results include failure analysis, spectral performance, durability testing, and manufacturing considerations for scaling durable silver coatings to large substrates.

Items.Authors: Reed L. Riddle, Christoph Baranec, James Ou, Luke McKay
Items.Title: Results of the commissioning and initial operations of the new Robo-AO 2 robotic observing system
Items.Abstract: The Robo-AO 2 system on the University of Hawai’i 2.2m telescope on Maunakea has been transitioning from commissioning to fully robotic operations during the past two years.  In that time, the Robo-AO team has commissioned both the laser guide star (LGS) and natural guide star (NGS) arms of the adaptive optics (AO) system, including a new real time control (RTC) and reconstructor system, an infrared camera system using a SAPHIRA detector, and the robotic observing system (ROS) that controls the hardware and executes science observations.  Progress has also been made on controlling the new adaptive secondary mirror (ASM) for the 88-inch, and on the hybrid AO system that blends LGS and NGS operations.  This presentation will discuss the results of the commissioning and early operations of the Robo-AO 2 software system, including an examination of the efficiency of robotic operations and of the operation of the AO system.

Items.Authors: Jordan Israel Diaz, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Philip M. Hinz, Daren Dillon, Pradip Gatkine, Aditya R. Sengupta, Dan Sirbu, Sarah A. Tedder, Kevin Bundy, Brian Vyhnalek, Steph Sallum, Matthew C. DeMartino, Stephen Eikenberry, Peter Delfyett, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa
Items.Title: Demonstrating the integration of a photonic lantern with an all-fiber-based nulling interferometer
Items.Abstract: High-contrast imaging of Solar System scale exoplanets and protoplanets demands advancements in instrumentation to access deeper starlight suppression at smaller angular separations than today's state-of-the-art. The multi-mode to single-mode conversion capabilities of photonic lanterns (PLs) provide new avenues to implement techniques such as nulling interferometry due to the inherent spatial filtering of single-mode waveguides. In this work, we present laboratory results on an all-fiber-based focal plane nulling interferometer using off-the-shelf components operating at 1550 nm. We demonstrate the implementation of a PL for coupling light into the instrument, and compare it to the case when laser light is directly fed into the interferometer. The integration of a PL with the interferometer evidences their potential for feeding photonic-based instruments. Additionally, we discuss expanding the concept of the instrument for the detection of accreting protoplanets.

Items.Authors: Babak Sedghi, Ulrich Lampater, Pablo Zuluaga, Juan-Carlos González-Herrera, Yannick Lammen, Michael Müller, Gerd Jakob, Veronika Wimmer
Items.Title: ESO ELT - vibration management: system level verification and monitoring
Items.Abstract: From early phases of the ELT programme different aspects of vibration managements such as modeling, error budgeting, requirement specifications, to envisaging verification and mitigation methods. During various phases of the project substantial effort was made to identify the sources of vibration through different contracts and to envisage various mitigation measures early in the in the design. Many of the identified sources could be measured and characterized in ESO vibration test facility. Other sources mainly those installed in dome and facilities in the observatory were identified and modeled. The data from identified sources is fed into the telescope system level model to estimate the telescope performance and compare it to the initial budget. A plan for vibration management and a method for system level verification on site as a monitoring system is envisaged and proposed. This paper presents the plan and the latest state of this monitoring system already in operation.

Items.Authors: Nicolas J. Flagey, Thomas Dutkiewicz, Kelly Coleman, Groebner Andy, Joshua Goldberg, Shireen Gonzaga, Sherie Holfeltz, Amy Jones, Katie Kaleida, Victoria Laidler, Lauretta Nagel, Andreea O. Petric, Sean Rapp, Christina Reitemeyer, Erik Tollerud
Items.Title: Integrating sustainability into early systems engineering for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aspires to answer a broad range of key questions in astronomy, including whether life exists beyond Earth. In the global sustainability context of the 2030s and 2040s, the credibility and impact of a space mission will also depend on demonstrating responsibility to the only habitable world we know.  We present a framework to integrate the environmental dimension of sustainability into early HWO development by tracking the carbon footprint of mission activities and treating a carbon budget as a formal engineering constraint, integrated with traditional budgets (e.g. mass, power, and cost) through their natural systems-level interdependencies.  This work identifies actionable practices, pathways to encourage stakeholders and partners, and lessons from other large-scale scientific enterprises. Our approach will position HWO as a technical, scientific, and ethical example: advancing space astronomy and meaningfully contributing to a sustainable future.

Items.Authors: Pietro Bolli, Marco Poloni, Luca Schirru, Alessandro Cabras, Giuseppe Carboni, Corrado Contavalle, Gianluca Esposito, Franco Fiocchi, Francesco Gaudiomonte, Federica Govoni, Adelaide Ladu, Sergio Mariotti, Pasqualino Marongiu, Emilio Molinari, Matteo Murgia, Carlo Nocita, Andrea Orlati, Pierluigi Ortu, Mauro Pili, Tonino Pisanu, Sergio Poppi, Teresa Pulvirenti, Juri Roda, Alessandro Scalambra, Gian Paolo Vargiu
Items.Title: Technical validation of the tri-band receivers at the INAF radio telescopes
Items.Abstract: The Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF) has procured three compact tri-band radio astronomy receivers developed by the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI). Designed for the Medicina, Noto, and Sardinia Radio Telescopes, these systems enable simultaneous observations between 18 and 116 GHz. Key features include dual-circular polarization, frequency-independent aperture efficiency, a high dynamic range for solar observations, and a 112 GHz instantaneous bandwidth split across three frequency bands, K, Q, W. Following delivery in 2022, major infrastructure upgrades were implemented on the antennas to support high-frequency and wideband operations. This paper describes the RF validation, antenna integration, lessons learned, and preliminary on-site testing.

Items.Authors: Chen Zhang, Ge Jin, Xiaojin Sun, Zhixing Ling, Yuan Liu, ZhiMing Cai, WeiMin Yuan
Items.Title: The performance of the lobster-eye telescope onboard Einstein Probe mission
Items.Abstract: The Einstein Probe (EP), dedicated to time-domain astronomy in the soft X-ray band, was launched in January 2024. Operating nominally under the leadership of the Chinese Academy of Sciences with international partners, EP achieves wide-field imaging via proven micro-pore lobster-eye (MPO) optics as well as large scientific CMOS array aboard the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT). In orbit, WXT delivers a 3,830 deg² field of view with <5′ (FWHM) angular resolution, reaching a 5σ sensitivity of ~2.6×10⁻¹¹ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² (0.5–4 keV, ~0.8 mCrab) in 1 ks.  Leveraging WXT’s MPO heritage, NAOC and North Night Vision Science & Technology Co., Ltd. have jointly developed and tested next-generation MPO modules for future missions. The preliminary test results are also reported in this work.

Items.Authors: Logan M. Foote, Chris Albert, Steven Hailey-Dunsheath, Jonathon Hunacek, Elijah Kane, Charles Bradford
Items.Title: Ultrasensitive Kilo-Pixel KID arrays for PRIMA FIRESS: array readout and crosstalk
Items.Abstract: The Far-Infrared Enhanced Survey Spectrometer (FIRESS) on the Probe Far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA) will deploy Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) in 1,008-pixel array formats. The PRIMA sensitivity requirement has been demonstrated with subsets of these arrays. Ongoing advancements in fabrication and readout now allow for the simultaneous operation of > 800 of these low-NEP pixels, meeting the FIRESS requirement.  To meet FIRESS science requirements, pixel-to-pixel crosstalk in the arrays should be controlled to the percent level or better. This includes effects on the chip (photons, spatial field effects) and due to readout (resonator overlap, electronics crosstalk). We mitigate these effects and demonstrate crosstalk performance with a combination of noise correlations and direct pair-wise signal crosstalk measurements.

Items.Authors: Roelof S. de Jong, Olga Bellido-Tirado, Joar G. Brynnel, Steffen Frey, Christine Füßlein, Domenico Giannone, Diana Johl, Ulrike Lemke, Genoveva Micheva, Allar Saviauk, Matthias Steinmetz, Weijia Sun, Jakob C. Walcher, Roland Winkler, Rosanna Sordo, Jonathan Loveday, Vincenzo Mainieri, Jean-François Pirard, Şenol Yazici, Wolfgang Gaessler, Florence Laurent, Andrea Merloni, Ramon Navarro, Alban Remillieux, Florian Rothmaier, Scott Smedley, Nicolas Walton
Items.Title: 4MOST: the 4-metre Multi-Object Spectroscopic Telescope project at the start of science operations
Items.Abstract: 4MOST is a new high-multiplex, wide-field spectroscopic survey facility for ESO's 4m-VISTA telescope at Paranal, Chile, that saw first light on October 18, 2025. Its key specifications are: a large field of view of 4.4 square degrees, a high multiplex fibre positioner based on the tilting spine principle positioning 2436 science fibres, 1624 fibres going to two low-resolution spectrographs (R = λ/Δλ ~ 6500), and 812 fibres transferring light to the high-resolution spectrograph (R ~ 20,000). The commissioning, data-flow operations rehearsal, and science verification phases shall be completed by Q2 2026 after which the facility will start its first 5-year survey consisting of 25 different science programmes. An overview will be given of instrument performance and the unique operational scheme of 4MOST.

Items.Authors: James F. Bosch, Timothy Jenness, Gregory P. Dubois-Felsmann
Items.Title: Challenges serializing Rubin Observatory data products
Items.Abstract: At the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory the image-based data products include data models that are not described by any existing FITS standard. These include spatially-varying point-spread functions, complex World Coordinate System models, provenance information, and shutter motion profiles. For DP1 these data models were written using generic C++ storage APIs resulting in files that can only easily be read using our software. For DP2 we have changed our approach so as to write FITS files that are more accessible by the community and can be accessed more efficiently from object stores. In this presentation we will describe our new approach to serializing data models and how it compares with the existing files, and our approach for improving object store access to individual extensions and integration with the Butler. We will also discuss whether we can expand our file format support to include alternatives such as HDF5, Zarr, and ASDF.

Items.Authors: Mary Angelie M. Alagao, Vincent Chambouleyron, Romain Fétick, Arnaud Striffling, Cédric Taïssir Héritier, Jean-François Sauvage, Mahawa Cisse, Mathieu Motte, Francisco Oyarzun, François Leroux, Matteo Pasinetti, Edvardas Vinerskas, Sylvain Cetre, David Barr, Eduard Muslimov, Alexis Carlotti, Steven Martos, Guillermo Martin, Noémie Mestre, François Huppert, François Dolon, Marc Ferrari, Benoît Neichel, Thierry Fusco
Items.Title: Four years of on-sky adaptive optics with PAPYRUS at OHP: performance and insights
Items.Abstract: PAPYRUS, which stands for the Provence Adaptive oPtics PYramid RUn System), is an on-sky, double-stage adaptive optics (AO) platform jointly developed by LAM and ONERA at the 1.52 m telescope of the Observatoire Haute Provence (OHP). Its primary goal is to push the technological developments in adaptive optics for the scientific community. Over nearly four years of on-sky operations, between June 2022 and March 2026, PAPYRUS has provided AO-assisted access to fiber-fed spectrographs, validated new AO concepts and control algorithms, and served as a hands-on teaching instrument for students. In this work, we review PAPYRUS’ performance and functions, discuss its operational limitations and facility, share lessons learned, and describe the mitigation strategies implemented. Finally, we introduce the next version of PAPYRUS that will soon be mounted on the Copernico Telescope in Asiago, Italy.

Items.Authors: Stefan Schwinde, Thomas Gischkat, Ralph Schlegel, Svetlana Shestaeva, Christian Mühlig, Sven Schröder, Nils Bartels, Moritz Vogel, Nicolas Steenbergen, Thomas Klumpp, Patric Seefeldt, Thomas Renger, Erik Klein, Frank Burmeister, Marina Paule, Christopher Jahn
Items.Title: Mirrors for the high-power laser communication terminals
Items.Abstract: Free-space optical laser communication is advancing rapidly, with future systems requiring higher-power lasers (up to 100 W) for improved data rates and longer-distance transmission to geostationary orbits. However, increased laser power poses risks of performance degradation due to light absorption effects. The presented work focuses on coatings for high-power laser communication.    The study employs various testing methods including absorption determination, laser damage testing, and space qualification tests. Conventional coating techniques and materials were used, considering high-volume production and cost reduction. Results indicate that specific coating-substrate combinations, such as Ag-based coatings on diamond-turned Al6061 substrates, show promise for laser communication systems.    The work is performed on behalf of the European Space Agency (Project “AO/1-11188/22/NL/FGL: High power coating development for space-based laser communication terminals”).

Items.Authors: Hele Savin, Olli Setälä, Ville Vähänissi, Oskari Leiviskä, Mariia Terletskaia, Joonas Isometsä, Joonas Viuho
Items.Title: Nanostructured photodiodes for improved sensitivity over wide spectral range
Items.Abstract: Elimination of reflective losses with conventional antireflection coatings (ARC) can be complicated / expensive. Furthermore, each wavelength region requires separately optimized ARC, i.e., one coating cannot be used for a wide spectral range. Nanotexturing the photodiode substrates, on the other hand, has recently been shown to eliminate the reflective losses over wide spectral range all the way to the cut-off wavelength - at least in Si, Ge and SiC. In this presentation we give an overview of recent advances in using nanostructures in photodiodes and their impact on device performance. The special emphasis will be on how these results could be utilized in astronomical applications.

Items.Authors: Stephen J. Williams
Items.Title: The "Flagstaff Solution" for Dark Skies
Items.Abstract: Ground-based astronomical observatories share the concern over  a growing threat: light pollution. Artificial Light At Night (ALAN) creates  skyglow that severely limits or completely inhibits an observatory's ability  to do science. For decades, the Flagstaff area’s dark skies have been preserved thanks to strong local ordinances. These lighting codes have been updated recently as the lighting industry transitions from bulb technology to LEDs. In discussing the “Flagstaff Solution” to the problem of ever-brightening night skies, we will discuss the technical aspects of the truly dark sky friendly lighting in Flagstaff, and how the decades of success in night sky preservation in and around Flagstaff can be applied everywhere.

Items.Authors: William S. Burgett, Rebecca Bernstein, Bruce Bigelow, Glenn Brossus, Marianne Cox, Richard Demers, Francisco Figueroa, Barbara Fischer, Frank Groark, Robert Laskin, Rafael Millan-Gabet, Samuel Park, Robert Ruggerio, Robert Turner, Brian Walls, King-Ming Lam
Items.Title: The Giant Magellan Telescope project in 2026: status and plan forward
Items.Abstract: The Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) is one of three planned ground-based optical/IR Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs). The GMT is now in the NSF Final Design Phase. A completed 8.4m diameter primary mirror segments was used to demonstrate excellent figure control with the GMT test mirror cell. The telescope mount azimuth structures continue fabrication. The first off-axis adaptive secondary mirror system has completed a second system level test program. A new adaptive optics testbed is being used to continue development of the GMT phasing strategy. Science instruments are in various development stages from design through early fabrication. Construction documents and drawings are undergoing final quality checks for the telescope enclosure bid packages. Hard rock excavation of the foundations for the enclosure and telescope pier is complete. Residence buildings and other facilities and infrastructure needed to support construction at the Las Campanas site in Chile are in operation.

Items.Authors: Alexandra Mavropoulou, Stephen Yates, Dimitry Lamers, Daniela Perez Capelo, Hendrik Veen, David Thoen, Jochem Baselmans, Shahab Dabironezare
Items.Title: A focal plane array of lens antenna coupled microwave kinetic inductance detectors with integrated polarizer for the PRIMAger polarimetric imager
Items.Abstract: The PRIMAger Polarimetric Imager (PPI), as part of the Probe Far Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA), is under development to provide astronomical maps of intensity and polarization. PPI will use Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) coupled to single polarized antennas, in the 80 to 264 μm range, using four sub-bands with each a 25% relative bandwidth. To measure the first three components of the Stokes vector (I,Q,U), i.e. total intensity and linearly polarized intensity simultaneously, the antennas are sequentially rotated towards three angles, separated by 120°. In this work, the radiation coupling mechanism of this instrument is presented, which is based on a focal plane array of tapered-slot leaky wave lens antennas, connected to the MKIDs via a coplanar waveguide, in which radiation detection takes place. To further reduce the cross polarized sensitivity of the instrument, an array of polarizing grids is integrated inside the lens array.

Items.Authors: Olivier Godet, Stéphane Schanne
Items.Title: First results from the SVOM/ECLAIRs GRB trigger camera
Items.Abstract: The Chinese-French space Gamma-ray burst mission SVOM launched in June 2024 is dedicated to high-energy transients, in particular Gamma-ray bursts. Those latter objects are thought to signal the catastrophic formation of a black hole or a neutron star and the launch of powerful ultra-relativistic jets oriented along our line of sight. SVOM embarks on an agile platform a suite of multi-wavelength instruments: 2 wide-field instruments to study the prompt phase from 4 keV up to 5 MeV and 2 narrow-field instruments to study the afterglow phase in both soft X-rays (0.3-10 keV) and optical (B and R bands). ECLAIRs is a 4-150 keV coded mask camera in charge of autonomously detecting HE transients within its FoV (2 sr) and providing their first localization. In this talk, I will present the SVOM mission and the main features of the ECLAIRs instrument along with its calibration. I will also highlight the instrument main performances and some science results.

Items.Authors: Scott C. Roberts, Keivan Ahmadi, Max Braun, Peter Byrnes, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Taz Oldaker, John Rogers, Matthias Schoeck
Items.Title: Integrated modeling and experimental validation of vibration effects on optical performance: development of an instrumented testbed
Items.Abstract: Vibration disturbances are a significant source of image degradation in astronomical instrumentation, especially when operating in adaptive optics mode. Natural guide star adaptive optics wavefront sensor bandwidth limits the correction of tip-tilt above approximately 5Hz. We develop the integrated modelling and virtual sensing framework required for feed-forward control based on accelerometer data. We present initial results of experimental modal analysis based on measured frequency response functions (FRF) between a modal exciter input and accelerometers located at each optical element. We predict the optical response to vibration input and compare acceleration values and measured tip-tilt on the wavefront sensor for the case of a stationary response and single tone force input.

Items.Authors: Raphaël Pourcelot, Laurent Pueyo, Rémi Soummer, Marshall D. Perrin, Emiel H. Por, Sarah Steiger, Randal Telfer
Items.Title: JWST telemetry combined with active coronagraphy: inferring raw contrast predictions for exoplanet imaging with future large space observatory
Items.Abstract: NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to detect and study Earth-like exoplanets, which will require maintaining some wavefront error mode at a picometric stability over hours. While the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) achieves sub-nanometer stability, it lacks the advanced coronagraphy and active wavefront control needed for direct imaging of such planets.  To better understand the technology gap to be bridged by HWO, we combine JWST’s segments phasing in-flight data, a modern Apodized Pupil Lyot Coronagraph (APLC) design, and wavefront control techniques from the Roman Space Telescope’s Coronagraph Instrument (CGI) to simulate residual wavefront errors under realistic conditions. We evaluate different system designs, including deformable mirror and sensor configurations, to determine achievable contrast levels. The pairing these simulations with JWST’s stability measurements provides insight of the current technological capabilities for Earth-like planet imaging.

Items.Authors: Mona El Morsy, Elizabeth Arcadi, Simon Gross, Stephanie Rossini-Bryson, Barnaby Norris, Glen Douglass, Peter Tuthill, Olivier Guyon, Julien Lozi, Thayne Currie, Sebastien Vievard, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Nemanja Jovanovic
Items.Title: Starlight suppression with photonic integrated circuits: laboratory characterization and future applications for Subaru/GLINT and HWO
Items.Abstract: Directly imaging Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars requires starlight suppression on the order of ~10⁻¹⁰ . Nulling interferometry offers a pathway to achieve this extreme level of suppression at small angular separations challenging to coronagraphs (~1–2 λ/D), by suppressing stellar light through destructive interference while transmitting off-axis planet light. Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) have emerged as compact, stable platforms for implementing nulling interferometers.  In this talk, we describe the laboratory characterization of one such application of PICs for GLINT on Subaru and HWO, tested at UTSA and developed by Macquarie University. Our design focuses on a photonic chip incorporating an integrated thermal phase shifter. We describe how this approach differs from that of conventional PICs, where the thermal phase shifter in our setup provides an active tuning to correct for optical path differences and thus sustaining deep null performance.

Items.Authors: Jongsoo Kim, Takashi Nakamoto, Jongsuk Hong, Makoto Shizugami, Isaac Goicovich, Camilo Saldias, Heesun Yoon, Won-Kee Park, Yaocheng Chen, Shun Ishii
Items.Title: Total power GPU spectrometer (TPGS) for the ALMA2030 wideband sensitivity upgrade
Items.Abstract: The Total Power GPU Spectrometer (TPGS) is being developed for ALMA’s 4-antenna Total Power array as part of the Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade, replacing the ACA Spectrometer. TPGS will process 4 digitized streams per antenna at 40 Gsps with 6-bit resolution, yielding a 3.84 Tbps input data rate—10 times larger than the current system—and a 32 GHz science bandwidth per polarization per antenna. To manage this data, TPGS utilizes 400 GbE, DPDK, and GPUDirect RDMA. To achieve a 13.5 kHz frequency resolution from 20 GHz wideband streams, a two-stage channelizer is implemented using an OverSampling Poly-phase Filter Bank (OSPFB) followed by a Critically Sampled Poly-phase Filter Bank (CSPFB). Pipelines benchmarked on NVIDIA GH200 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs achieved real-time execution times for 16.0 ms data durations (15.2 ms and 13.2 ms for single-stream; 22.4 ms and 23.8 ms for dual-stream). Spectral outputs were verified using sinusoidal signals on Gaussian noise.

Items.Authors: Karl Fleury-Frenette, Cédric Lénaerts, Frédéric Rabecki, Camille Galy, Aline Hermans, Cédric Thizy
Items.Title: PROBA3 ASPIICS coronograph internal occulter multifunctional coating
Items.Abstract: We present the mutifunctional coating designed for the internal occulter of the ASPIICS (Association of Spacecraft for Polarimetric and Imaging Investigation of the Corona of the Sun) instrument. ASPIICS is the primary payload of the ESA PROBA-3 mission, an in-orbit demonstration of precise formation flying for future European missions. The instrument is based on an externally occulted Lyot coronograph with the particularity of being distributed over two spacecrafts approximately 150 m apart. The internal occulter consists in a precisely positioned patterned coating applied on the planar side of a plano-convex field lens; it features an opaque ring surrounded by a highly transparent outer ring and an inner clear aperture over the range 528 nm – 590 nm. The coating design and performance are presented here along with details on its patterning and positioning on the lens.

Items.Authors: Axel Potier, Célia Desgrange, Raphaël Galicher, Johan Mazoyer, Pierre Baudoz, Zahed Wahhaj
Items.Title: Coherent differential imaging on VLT/SPHERE: first results and beyond
Items.Abstract: High-contrast imaging relies on advanced coronagraphs and adaptive optics (AO) to suppress starlight. Yet, residual aberrations—particularly non-common path aberrations —still constrain instrument performance. Standard post-processing methods, such as angular differential imaging or spectral differential imaging, can mitigate these effects but they are prone to self-subtraction at small angular separations.  Coherent differential imaging (CDI) offers a promising alternative. Through speckle modulation, CDI isolates coherent starlight residuals, enabling their subtraction during post-processing. In previous work, we validated a CDI method on real science targets observed with VLT/SPHERE, demonstrating its effectiveness in imaging circumstellar disks. In this presentation, we present further progress, including parallelized multi-wavelength calibration using the SPHERE Integral Field Spectrograph and the mitigation of residual dynamic speckles through wavefront sensor telemetry.

Items.Authors: Angaraj Duara, Jesper Skottfelt, Chiaki Crews, David Hall, Ben Dryer, Joan Requena, Anabel Romero, Douglas Jordan
Items.Title: Quantum efficiency measurement of enhanced coating CMOS detectors for future UV space missions
Items.Abstract: Future UV space telescopes such as the NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), will require detectors with high quantum efficiency across the UV wavelength range. Although CMOS Image Sensors (CIS) now dominate space instrumentation due to their radiation tolerance, low power consumption, and fast readout, their UV response is limited by the shallow absorption depths and reflection losses of UV photons. To address this, several UV-enhancement technologies have been developed. This work presents a comparative study of three such technologies applied to the CIS120 devices from Teledyne e2v; NASA/JPL’s Delta Doping, Teledyne e2v’s UV-enhanced coating, and Aalto University/Elfys’ black-silicon Technology. Using a bespoke UV test facility at the CEI Open University, we evaluate and compare their quantum efficiencies to assess suitability for future UV missions.

Items.Authors: David Heffernan-Clarke, Sebastian Buntin, Iain Steele, Helen Jermak, Chris Copperwheat, David Copley, Robert Smith
Items.Title: Shutter to science: upgrading data pipelines for the Liverpool telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the design of an integrated, cloud-based data pipeline for the Liverpool Telescope to replace the legacy  on premises service. We give an end-to-end view of how raw images and telemetry flow from the summit to long-  term archive and back to astronomers. The Science Operations Data Centre coordinates message-driven workflows and cloud storage to deliver robust data ingestion, automated calibration, provenance tracking and the generation  of science-ready data products (SDPs) suitable for immediate use. We focus on the data reduction pipelines:  how calibration data are managed, how processing histories are recorded, and how we ensure that outputs remain  reproducible as instruments evolve and survey volume increases. The pipelines tolerate intermittent connectivity,  preserving data integrity and eventual delivery while still providing useful feedback on system state.

Items.Authors: Joanna Rosenbluth, Ramya Anche, Nikoli Cooper, Kyle Van Gorkom, William Melby, Daewook Kim, Ewan Douglas
Items.Title: Design and modeling of an oblique incidence dichroic mirror for a high contrast imaging system
Items.Abstract: The proposed Habitable Worlds Observatory aims to detect and characterize Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars from the ultraviolet to the infrared using high-contrast imaging. A dichroic mirror is a natural choice for splitting light between multiple wavelength channels in such a system, but the coating must introduce minimal polarization aberrations and chromatic wavefront errors to avoid limiting contrast. We present the design of a long-pass dichroic mirror operated at a 7° AOI that provides high reflection from 400-540nm and high transmission from 560-750nm. A multilayer thin-film design process was used to meet these spectral requirements while reducing polarization aberrations and chromatic WFE sensitivity. The resulting coating-induced WFE was propagated through simulations of a VVC to assess contrast performance. Simulations predict dark-hole contrast residuals at the 10^(−12) level, indicating that the optimized dichroic mirror does not limit coronagraph performance.

Items.Authors: Stéphane Schanne
Items.Title: Design of the ECLAIRs trigger for SVOM gamma-ray burst detection
Items.Abstract: The French-Chinese SVOM satellite (Space Variable Objects Monitor), launched in June 2024, with is designed to study astrophysical transient events, among which primarily Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs). The ECLAIRs Trigger of the hard X-ray coded-mask instrument ECLAIRs onboard SVOM autonomously localizes the bursts and requests the satellite to slew to those sources for follow-up observations by the onboard instruments MXT and VT and transmits real-time alerts to the ground, for further follow-up campaigns. This paper presents the ECLAIRs Trigger, including the design of both trigger algorithms running simultaneously onboard, the Count-Rate Trigger (CRT) and the Image Trigger (IMT). The ECLAIRs Trigger has permitted the detection of several notable GRBs, including classical as well as peculiar X-ray rich GRBs, including some high-redshift GRBs. After description of the algorithms the paper will give a summary on the most notable results obtained in flight.

Items.Authors: Maria Grazia Labate, Grazia Umana, Ugo Di Giammatteo, Corrado Trigilio, Pietro Bolli, Andrea Melis, Francesco Schillirò, Francesco Cavallaro, Enrico Giro, Rodolfo Canestrari, Adriano Fontana, Gianfranco Fallica, Tonino Pisanu, Pasqualino Marongiu, Carolina Belli, Kobus Cloete, Sipho Ngunyule, Sibongile Nong, Scarre Celliers, Sias Malan, Ruan de Lange, Renier Siebrits, Wesley Newton, Tyrone van Balla, George Isoe, Ofaletse Mokone, Marc Welz, Hendrik Bester, Ben Jordaan
Items.Title: Enabling High-Frequency Capability on the MeerKAT Radio Telescope in the SKA Era: The STILES MeerKAT Band 5B Project
Items.Abstract: The MeerKAT Band 5B project will extend the telescope’s high-frequency capability by deploying 64 newly developed cryogenic receivers, along with down-convertering digitizers, backend systems, and supporting infrastructure.  Operating in the SKA-Mid Band 5b range (8.3–15.4 GHz), this upgrade will make MeerKAT the most sensitive centimeter-wave interferometer in the southern hemisphere until SKA becomes fully operational. Since MeerKAT currently lacks access to these frequencies and SKAO will not retrofit band 5 onto the MeerKAT antennas, this project uniquely enables capability that would otherwise not be realized, providing Band 5B ahead of time and serving as a technological and scientific precursor.   Designed to meet SKA specifications, Band 5B ensures sustained scientific value into the SKA era.  All procurement activities have been completed. By November 2025, all receivers had been manufactured and almost fully delivered to site, and all 64 digitizer D-Engines manufactured and test

Items.Authors: Sébastien B. Vievard, Elsa Huby, Sylvestre Lacour, Olivier Guyon, Manon Lallement, Mathias Nowak, Yoo Jung Kim, Aidan Walk, Jehanne Sarrazin, Sergio Leon-Saval, Christopher Betters, Julien Lozi, Miles Lucas, Vincent Deo, Michael Fitzgerald, Barnaby Norris, Thayne Currie, Guy Perrin
Items.Title: FIRST-PL: commissioning the first visible photonic lantern spectrograph for sub-diffraction-limit astronomy on Subaru/SCExAO
Items.Abstract: FIRST-PL (Fibered Imager foR a Single Telescope - Photonic Lantern) is a newly commissioned visible-light instrument on Subaru/SCExAO achieving spectroscopy below the diffraction limit. The instrument uses a Photonic Lantern—converting multimode fiber into 19 single-mode outputs—feeding a mid-resolution spectrograph (R~3000, 630-790 nm). On-sky performance demonstrates 40% injection efficiency at 680 nm (Strehl ~30%) and 12× throughput improvement over single-mode fibers. Three operational modes enable spectro-astrometry (50 microarcsecond precision demonstrated on β-CMi), image reconstruction, and high-contrast imaging (contrast ~1000 at 100 mas). Science applications include mapping evolved star environments, resolving close binaries, and detecting Hα emission from accreting protoplanets. FIRST-PL represents a significant advancement in high-throughput photonic instrumentation for ultra-high-resolution astronomical imaging.

Items.Authors: José L. Ortiz, Jaime Robles, Jorge Avarias, Ricardo Carrasco, Johnny Reveco, Sebastian Rodriguez, Gastón Vélez, Jose Lobos, Baltasar Vila-Vilaro, Javier Rojas, Vicente Aitken, Jason Castro
Items.Title: Managing critical and large-scale obsolescence at ALMA: the E2C deployment project
Items.Abstract: The ALMA Observatory, with 66 radiotelescopes and other central systems, has operated for nearly 15 years and is undergoing major upgrades while needing to maintain aging infrastructure. The Ethernet-To-CAN (E2C) project addressed obsolescence by replacing ALMA’s legacy real-time control computers. This paper focuses on the E2C Deployment Project, covering the manufacturing, installation, testing, and acceptance of the new devices. As ALMA’s first observatory-wide hardware upgrade, the deployment had to be completed during record observing output, tightly aligned with the Cycle 12 software release, and fully compliant with new cybersecurity requirements. Despite these constraints, the project finished on schedule and with minimal operational impact thanks to detailed planning, early risk and failure mitigation, extensive unit and system validation, and disciplined yet adaptable execution.

Items.Authors: Breann N. Sitarski, Theodore J. Hadjimichael, George M. Hilton, Babak N. Saif, David Baran, Michael J. Eisenhower, Sang Park, Marcel Bluth, James M. Whipple, Stephen P. Chaykovsky, Stephen J. Hagopian, Elliot C. Schwartz, Jordan M. Effron, Michael Chapman, Brian S. Abresch, Dawn L. Blackburn, Thomas P. Zielinski, Brooke Turner, Colby D. Moore
Items.Title: Mini-Metrology and Ultra-Stable Testbed (Mini-MUST): a TRL-advancing stability testbed for Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) requires unprecedented, picometer-level stability to fulfill one of its driving science requirements of detecting and characterizing Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars. Over the last several years, the Goddard Space Flight Center’s Ultra-Stable Structures Laboratory has been designing and constructing the Mini-Metrology and Ultra-Stable Testbed (Mini-MUST) to test components and systems to these stability levels and advance their technical readiness levels. Mini-MUST recently achieved first light at GSFC and has started testing campaigns to support the ROSES D.19 projects. We present our first light results, including correlation of our measured data with our high-fidelity thermal and structural models.

Items.Authors: Fengchuan Liu
Items.Title: Progress update on the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) project
Items.Abstract: TMT is an extremely large optical-infrared telescope (ELT) with diffraction-limited performance, the only ELT in the northern hemisphere. As part of the US ELT program, TMT received the top ranking in Astro2020 and passed the NSF PDR in 2023. A December 2024 report from a NSF external review on US ELT recommended entering TMT to NSF final design phase. The US President's FY2026 Budget Request to Congress, however, left TMT outside of the NSF final design process. This presented a significant challenge in the path forward and to the progress TMT has made in building relationships with communities in Hawaii. Members of TMT International Observatory remain committed in finding a path forward, including evaluating a generous offer from the Government of Spain to build the observation in Spain. This paper will describe the latest technical progress in TMT’s design and development in all partner countries, and the many challenges and opportunities of managing a truly global collaboration.

Items.Authors: Elijah Kane, Chris Albert, Andrew Beyer, Charles Bradford, Pierre Echternach, Logan Foote, Jason Glenn, Henry LeDuc, Jonas Zmuidzinas
Items.Title: Ultrasensitive kilo-pixel kinetic inductance detector arrays for PRIMA FIRESS: preserving sensitivity in the space radiation environment
Items.Abstract: The Probe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA) is a proposed space observatory at wavelengths between 25 and 265 microns. Kinetic inductance detector (KID) arrays fabricated for PRIMA at the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory have achieved background-limited sensitivities for the space environment. In this talk, I summarize the yield and sensitivity of prototype arrays for PRIMA’s spectrometer, FIRESS. I also discuss the measures taken to qualify the arrays for use in the energetic proton environment of the L2 orbit. We demonstrate that a backside metal layer is effective in reducing cosmic ray glitch rates and infer a dead time due to proton impacts of well below 10%. We have also performed an experiment to demonstrate that total dose is not a concern for aluminum KIDs. We cryogenically irradiate the array with alpha particles to many times the expected total displacement damage dose in PRIMA’s 5-year lifetime, finding no change in performance.

Items.Authors: Maren Cosens, Nicholas P. Konidaris, Gwen C. Rudie, Andrew B. Newman, Leon Aslan, Robert Barkhouser, Christoph Birk, Julia Brady, Mathias Gumy, Tyson Hare, Stephen C. Hope, Charlie Hull, Karim Kaismoune, Daniel D. Kelson, Gerrad Killion, Alicia Lanz, Jacob McCloskey, Solange Ramirez, Cyril Rupf, William Schoenell, Patricio Schurter, Stephen A. Smee, Peter Spanoudakis, Jason E. Williams
Items.Title: Update on the Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS)
Items.Abstract: The Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS) will be a next generation multi-object (MOS) and integral field spectrograph (IFS) for the 6.5m Magellan telescopes at Las Campanas Observatory in Chile. MIRMOS will perform R~3700 spectroscopy over a simultaneous wavelength range of 0.886 - 2.404um (Y, J, H, and K bands) in addition to imaging over the range of 0.7 - 0.886um. Target selection in the MOS mode is achieved through a cryogenic mechanism capable of making up to 92 slits over a 13’x3’ field of view (FoV). The IFS mode of operation for MIRMOS will be achieved via an image slicer style integral field unit (IFU) which provides an ~18”x26” FoV made up of 0.84”x26” slices. We will describe here the design of the MIRMOS instrument -- now at the end of the preliminary design phase.

Items.Authors: Matthijs Mars, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Joseph D. Long, Rico Landman, Louis Desdoigts, Olivier Guyon, Jared R. Males, Laird M. Close, Kyle van Gorkum, Alexander D. Hedglen, Sandrine Juillard
Items.Title: Physics-informed digital twin for forward modelling low-order aberrations in high-contrast imaging
Items.Abstract: We develop a physics-informed, fully differentiable digital twin of a high-contrast imager’s science path and low-order wavefront sensor to forward-model residual low-order aberrations and reconstruct the stellar PSF. By explicitly modelling the aberrations measured by the LOWFS, the approach improves stellar leakage subtraction compared to methods that rely solely on science camera data. This hybrid physics/data framework improves robustness, reduces calibration requirements, and adapts easily to different coronagraph configurations. We present initial laboratory validation on MagAO-X, demonstrating the feasibility of telemetry-driven forward modelling.

Items.Authors: William J. Marshall, Henry Corbett, Shannon Fitton, Megan Dubay, Nicholas M. Law, Thomas Procter, Alan Vasquez Soto, Jonah L. Aponte, Alex Bucheli, Jonathan Carney, Thomas Cowart, James Dockery, Katie M. Fasbender, Collin H. Grimes, Amy S. Ishiguro, Lawrence Machia, Michael Ronco, Donovan Schlekat, Glenn Walters
Items.Title: Electron umbrellas and photon rain: An investigation into several noise and charge effects in CMOS detectors
Items.Abstract: Astronomical surveys like the upcoming Argus Array, a 1,200-telescope optical survey instrument which will image 8,000 square degrees every minute, rely on the combination of many images from CMOS detectors to meet their scientific objectives. It is therefore important to know exactly how the images from these detectors behave when stacked. Here, we show that certain artifacts, which may not cause issues in single frames, could become relevant when large numbers of these images are co-added for additional depth. We have conducted an investigation into the behavior of one such class of artifact, here referred to as “umbrellas” for their shape, and their potential impact on image calibration and co-addition. These artifacts appear 100s of times in every Sony IMX455 and IMX461 image we examined and pollute 10-15 nearby pixels each. We discuss hot pixel detection methods and calibration routines which will mitigate the impact of these artifacts on Argus science products.

Items.Authors: Anastasia Galkin, Kirill Makan, Wail Abbas Ahmed, Ole Streicher, Simeon Reusch
Items.Title: The 4MOST public archive (4PA)
Items.Abstract: The Research Data Infrastructure group at the Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics  Potsdam (AIP) is leading the implementation of the 4MOST Public Archive (4PA),  the archive for processed and science-ready products from the 4-metre  Multi-Object Spectroscopic Telescope. 4PA is built on the Daiquiri publication  framework and deployed with the containerized dq-dev environment. The archive  will publish Level 1 spectra and Level 2 science products, initially to the  4MOST science community and later publicly according to the agreed release  policy.  This contribution describes the practical implementation of 4PA: the path from  provider-curated release tables and associated files to an access-controlled  archive, the use of metadata curation as the basis for web and  Virtual Observatory (VO) access, the deployment model, and 4PA-specific user  interfaces such as survey search, object pages, spectrum pages, file download,  and scripted Table Access Protocol (TAP) access.

Items.Authors: Joost A. van den Born, Rico Landman, David S. Doelman, Frans Snik, Yuki Nishie, Yuta Watanabe, Masakazu Shoda, Felix Bettonvil, Ester Aranzana, Jeroen Rietjens, Pierre Baudoz, Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Dennis Dolkens, Thomas Wijnen
Items.Title: Vector apodizing phase plates for the ELT: from prototype to final optics for METIS and MICADO
Items.Abstract: The first generation of instruments for the upcoming Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) will allow for the direct imaging of many exoplanets that were previously below the sensitivity or resolution limits of existing facilities. Three different Vector Apodizing Phase Plates, a liquid crystal based pupil coronagraph, will be available in both first light instruments; two in METIS, the mid-infrared imaging and spectroscopy instrument, and one in MICADO, the near infrared imaging instrument. In this work, we will present an overview of the current status of these optics, including the manufacturing, lab measurements and discuss the expected final performance.

Items.Authors: Mayukh Bagchi, Felix M. Thiel, Laura M. Fissel, Maggie Oxford, Lindy L. Blackburn, Rafael Costa, Vincent L. Fish, Daryl Haggard, Michael D. Johnson, Dominic W. Pesce, Ganesh Rajagopalan, Javier L. Romualdez, Aarchi Shah, Adrian K. Sinclair, Stephanie St-Jean, Terry Yang
Items.Title: An RFSoC-based backend and timing system for the balloon‑borne very long baseline interferometry experiment
Items.Abstract: We present a novel RFSoC-based digital backend and precision timing system for the Balloon-borne Very Long Baseline Interferometry Experiment (BVEX), a 22 GHz pathfinder mission for future high-frequency stratospheric mobile VLBI stations. The system employs an AMD-Xilinx RFSoC 4x2 for a high-resolution spectrometer and real-time 2-bit requantization of 4.096 GSPS sampled data, streaming at 8.2 Gbps via 100 Gigabit Ethernet to a 16 TB NVMe storage array. Timing stability is maintained by a Rakon OCXO with continuous GPS-based drift monitoring at 60-picosecond resolution. Ground testing validated system performance, demonstrating exceptional timing stability despite platform dynamics. This represents the first deployment of RFSoC-based VLBI instrumentation and precise timing systems on balloon platforms. For the 2027 reflight, we are implementing enhanced thermal management and expanded storage capacity, along with direct NIC to NVMe firmware, for improved power efficiency.

Items.Authors: Shahab O. Dabironezare, Giulia Conenna, Daan Roos, Dimitry Lamers, Daniela Perez Capelo, Hendrik M. Veen, David J. Thoen, Vishal Anvekar, Stephen J. C. Yates, Robert Huiting, Jochem J. A. Baselmans
Items.Title: Experimental demonstration of the optical coupling for an array of lens-absorber coupled KIDs operating at 6.98 THz for PRIMA
Items.Abstract: Focal plane arrays of silicon lenses with distributed absorbers coupled to Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) are the chosen detector technology for the hyperspectral imager of the PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA). In this contribution we present the modelling approach, design, fabrication, and experimental verification for a 25-pixel lens-absorber KID array operating at the central frequency of 6.98 THz. The aperture efficiency of the detectors is measured to be 54%. We verified this against numerical simulations using an in-house developed efficient spectral technique and find an excellent agreement. The noise equivalent power of the KIDs is also measured with a limiting value of 8×10^(-20)W/√Hz under negligible optical loading. These experimental verifications indicate that the modelling, design, realisation and characterisation of the proposed detectors are well understood, paving the way for the development of the flight chips for PRIMA’s hyperspectral imager.

Items.Authors: Hangxin Ji, Ru Chen, Yong Li, Cheng Liao, Haoran Yu, Jun Li, Qinyang Dong, Lei Wang
Items.Title: Multi-object fiber spectrograph for the 4-m class Jiao Tong University Spectroscopic Telescope (JUST)
Items.Abstract: The JUST telescope is a 4-m class, wide-field segmented facility dedicated to massively multiplexed spectroscopy. We present the optical and system design of its Multi-Object Fiber Spectrograph (MOFS), supporting up to 2,000 fibers across a 1.2° Nasmyth field. The instrument employs a three-channel layout (365–560nm, 540–745nm, 720–925nm) using dichroics, high-efficiency VPH gratings, and fast f/1.4 cameras fed by a 175-mm collimated beam. With optimized fiber-slit geometry, MOFS delivers R≈2,000–5,000 and >60% peak throughput. Each exposure records over 500 spectra and scales to the full survey capacity. One spectrograph also accommodates a compact 19-fiber IFU for spatially resolved studies of transients and compact objects. Engineered for stability at the 4,300-m site and optimized for faint targets, MOFS will enable dense mapping of large-scale structures, time-domain follow-ups, and coordinated surveys with WFST and CSST, advancing JUST as a next-generation spectroscopic facility.
